key_insight: LuxRemix decomposes complex indoor illumination from a single multi-view capture into individual light sources, enabling intuitive per-light editing (on/off, color, intensity) while enforcing multi-view consistent harmonization for realistic relighting.
problem_solved: Interactive, per-light editing of indoor scenes is hard because scene illumination is entangled and edits must remain consistent across viewpoints; LuxRemix provides a factorized representation that isolates light sources for independent manipulation and coherent multi-view rendering.
method: Generative image-based light decomposition that factorizes scene illumination into constituent light sources from a single multi-view capture.
Per-source controls for state (on/off), chromaticity, and intensity to enable targeted edits.
Multi-view lighting harmonization and rendering to ensure consistent appearance, shadows, and reflections across all views after edits.
impact: Makes realistic, interactive relighting and light-level editing practical for applications in AR/VR, interior design, and content creation; simplifies workflows for ML practitioners needing controllable scene illumination in downstream tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: capture → light decomposition → per-light editing controls → harmonized multi-view render outputs.
Before/after comparison gallery showing original vs. edited lighting (on/off, color shifts, intensity changes) with preserved geometry and shadows.
Per-source light maps / masks overlaid on the scene to visualize decomposed light contributors and their spatial influence.
UI mockup with toggles and sliders for each light source (on/off, color wheel, intensity) demonstrating interactive editing.
paper_title: LuxRemix: Lighting Decomposition and Remixing for Indoor Scenes
paper_authors: Ruofan Liang, Norman Müller, Ethan Weber, Duncan Zauss, Nandita Vijaykumar
